exposure: maternal secondhand smoke (SHS) exposure during pregnancy
outcome: wheezing phenotypes in children (never wheezing, early transient wheezing, late-onset wheezing, persistent wheezing)
cohort: The study analyzed 73,057 singleton births from pregnant women recruited from 15 regional centers in the Japan Environment and Children's Study.
finding: Maternal smoking before and throughout pregnancy, as well as maternal exposure to secondhand smoke during pregnancy, were significantly associated with an increased risk of early transient and persistent wheezing in children up to 3 years of age.
